newsitem.title: INDIA: India 97/98 crude output seen at 34.42 mln tonnes.
newsitem.headline: India 97/98 crude output seen at 34.42 mln tonnes.

text.p: India's crude oil output in 1997/98 (April/March) is expected to rise to 34.42 million tonnes from an estimated 33.43 million tonnes in 1996/97, a Petroleum Ministry statement said on Tuesday.
India's crude output in 1995/96 was 35.35 million tonnes, the highest level reached so far.
Crude oil import in 1996/97 was expected to be around 33.15 million tonnes as compared to 27.34 million in 1995/96, the statement quoted the ministry's 1996/97 annual report as saying.
It said the import of petroleum products in 1996/97 was also expected to be higher at 22.01 million tonnes, compared with 20.34 million in the previous year.
Export of petroleum products in 1996/97 was expected to be around 2.43 million tonnes, the statement said.

The statement said in 1996/97 hydrocarbons were discovered at 12 places including fields at Bombay offshore, Krishna-Godavari and cauvery basin in southern India and upper Assam in the northeastern region.
It said the cumulative refinery throughput between April-December, 1996 was 46.85 million tonnes, compared with installed capacity of 45.51 million tonnes.
The statement said the annual refining capacity was expected to grow to about 130 million tonnes in 2002 from the present 60.6 million tonnes.
India's demand for petroleum products by the end of 2002 is expected to grow to 113 million tonnes.
